# Summary of Lynn Conway
Lynn Conway (1938–2024) was a pioneering computer scientist and transgender activist. After studying electrical engineering at Columbia University, she joined IBM Research in 1964, contributing to the design of an advanced supercomputer and inventing key techniques in out-of-order dynamic instruction scheduling. Following her gender transition in 1968, which led to her dismissal from IBM, Conway stealthily rebuilt her career, working at Memorex and then leading the "LSI Systems" group at Xerox PARC. There, she co-developed the landmark Mead–Conway VLSI design methodology and founded the multiproject wafers (MPW) technology and MOSIS infrastructure, revolutionizing integrated circuit design and education worldwide. She also taught VLSI design at MIT and later held academic and leadership roles at the University of Michigan.
In transgender rights activism, Conway used her platform to provide resources, advocate for employment protections, and challenge stigmatizing theories. She publicly shared her transition story starting in 1999 and was recognized by various organizations for her influence. Conway received numerous awards, including IEEE Fellowship, membership in the National Academy of Engineering, and induction into the Computer History Museum and National Inventors Hall of Fame. IBM publicly apologized and honored her with a Lifetime Achievement Award in 2020. She passed away in 2024 at age 86.
